title: The Miller of the Dee
author: James Baldwin
summary: 快乐的磨坊主告诉国王：自食其力、家人相爱、无债一身轻，就是幸福。
publicDomainBasis: Published 1896 by the American Book Company; author James Baldwin (1841–1925). Public domain in the United States and in China (author's life plus 70 years).

paragraphs.en: Once upon a time there lived on the banks of the River Dee a miller, who was the happiest man in England. He was always busy from morning till night, and he was always singing as merrily as any lark. He was so cheerful that he made everybody else cheerful; and people all over the land liked to talk about his pleasant ways. At last the king heard about him.
paragraphs.zh: 从前，迪河岸边住着一位磨坊主，他是全英格兰最快乐的人。他从早忙到晚，总是像云雀一样欢快地唱歌。他的快乐感染了身边的每个人，全国各地的人都喜欢谈论他和善的性情。最后，国王也听说了他。

paragraphs.en: "I will go down and talk with this wonderful miller," he said. "Perhaps he can tell me how to be happy."
paragraphs.zh: “我要下去和这位了不起的磨坊主聊聊，”国王说，“也许他能告诉我怎样才能快乐。”

paragraphs.en: As soon as he stepped inside of the mill, he heard the miller singing:
paragraphs.zh: 国王刚一踏进磨坊，就听见磨坊主在唱：

paragraphs.en: "I envy nobody—no, not I!— For I am as happy as I can be; And nobody envies me."
paragraphs.zh: “我不羡慕任何人——不，一点也不！——因为我快乐得不能再快乐；而且没有人羡慕我。”

paragraphs.en: "You're wrong, my friend," said the king. "You're wrong as wrong can be. I envy you; and I would gladly change places with you, if I could only be as lighthearted as you are."
paragraphs.zh: “你错了，朋友，”国王说，“你错得不能再错了。我羡慕你；只要我能像你一样无忧无虑，我愿意和你交换位置。”

paragraphs.en: The miller smiled, and bowed to the king.
paragraphs.zh: 磨坊主笑了笑，向国王鞠了一躬。

paragraphs.en: "I am sure I could not think of changing places with you, sir," he said.
paragraphs.zh: “先生，我可绝不会想和您交换位置。”他说。

paragraphs.en: "Now tell me," said the king, "what makes you so cheerful and glad here in your dusty mill, while I, who am king, am sad and in trouble every day."
paragraphs.zh: “那你告诉我，”国王说，“你在这满是灰尘的磨坊里，为什么这么快乐开朗；而我身为国王，却每天忧愁烦恼？”

paragraphs.en: The miller smiled again, and said, "I do not know why you are sad, but I can easily tell why I am glad. I earn my own bread; I love my wife and my children; I love my friends, and they love me; and I owe not a penny to any man. Why should I not be happy? For here is the River Dee, and every day it turns my mill; and the mill grinds the corn that feeds my wife, my babes, and me."
paragraphs.zh: 磨坊主又笑了，说：“我不知道您为什么忧愁，但我很容易说清我为什么快乐。我靠自己挣饭吃；我爱我的妻子和孩子；我爱我的朋友，他们也爱我；我不欠任何人一分钱。我为什么不快乐呢？你看，迪河就在这里，它每天转动我的磨坊；磨坊磨出面粉，养活我的妻子、孩子和我。”

paragraphs.en: "Say no more," said the king. "Stay where you are, and be happy still. But I envy you. Your dusty cap is worth more than my golden crown. Your mill does more for you than my kingdom can do for me. If there were more such men as you, what a good place this world would be! Good-by, my friend!"
paragraphs.zh: “别说了，”国王说，“你就待在这里，继续快乐下去吧。可我羡慕你。你那顶落满灰尘的帽子，比我的金冠更值钱。你的磨坊给你的，比我的王国给我的还多。要是世上多些像你这样的人，这个世界该多好！再见，朋友！”

paragraphs.en: The king turned about, and walked sadly away; and the miller went back to his work singing:
paragraphs.zh: 国王转过身，黯然离去；磨坊主回去干活，嘴里唱着：

paragraphs.en: "Oh, I'm as happy as happy can be, For I live by the side of the River Dee!"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我快乐得不能再快乐，因为我住在迪河岸边！”
